The number of ways is $2^5 - 2 = 30$.

Each of the 5 elements is assigned to one of two distinguishable (ordered) subsets. This gives $2^5 = 32$ assignments. We subtract the 2 cases where all elements go to the same subset (leaving the other empty), leaving $32 - 2 = 30$.

Equivalently, using Stirling numbers of the second kind: $S(5,2) = 15$ counts unordered partitions into 2 non-empty blocks, and multiplying by $2!$ for the ordering of the blocks gives $2 \times 15 = 30$.

\boxed{30}
